title: Dialog
summary: A dependency-free modal with native focus handling, keyboard dismissal, and a small CSS token surface.
overview: A progressively enhanced modal built on the native dialog element. The live example runs the exact stored HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in an isolated browser session.

component.useWhen: Use a modal when a focused decision or short task must be completed before returning to the current page.
component.avoidWhen: Avoid it for passive information, long forms, multi-step flows, or content that deserves its own page.

variants.title: Responsive sizes
variants.summary: Small, medium, and large dialog widths selected by the trigger and capped to the viewport.
variants.useWhen: Use explicit sizes when different tasks need predictable reading widths but should share one dialog behavior.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid size choices based only on visual preference; let the content and task complexity determine the width.
customization: Change --dialog-size-sm, --dialog-size-md, and --dialog-size-lg without touching the controller.
The max-width cap keeps every size inside narrow preview and device viewports.
Each trigger declares its size with data-dialog-size, keeping behavior hooks out of styling classes.

example.title: Choose a dialog size
example.description: Open each size, then switch the preview to mobile to see every option respect the same viewport gutter.

source.html:
Responsive size

A width for the task

The controller changes a data attribute. CSS owns the width and always reserves a safe viewport gutter.

variants.title: Inner scroll
variants.summary: A viewport-bounded dialog whose header and actions stay visible while only the body scrolls.
variants.useWhen: Use inner scrolling when content can grow but the title, close control, and actions must remain continuously available.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid putting an entire long page or multi-step workflow inside a modal; move substantial work to a dedicated route.
customization: The dialog uses a three-row grid; only .c-dialog__content has overflow: auto.
Change --dialog-max-height to reserve more or less vertical viewport space.
Keep the heading outside the scroll region so the dialog context never disappears.

example.title: Scrollable terms dialog
example.description: Scroll the content and confirm that the title and decision buttons remain anchored.

source.html:
Before continuing

Review the terms

1. Your workspace

Your saved components remain in your project and can be exported whenever you need them.

2. Shared recipes

Only publish source you are allowed to share. Record the origin and license of every adapted pattern.

3. Preview sessions

Examples execute inside an isolated frame without network access, storage access, or navigation privileges.

4. Maintenance

Recheck keyboard behavior, narrow layouts, and browser support whenever a recipe changes.

5. Responsibility

Copied recipes are starting points. Validate security, accessibility, and product requirements before shipping.

variants.title: Maximizable
variants.summary: A dialog that can expand to the preview viewport and return to its original dimensions.
variants.useWhen: Use maximize for dense inspectors, tables, or editors that benefit from temporary extra space.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid it for short confirmations, where a fullscreen control adds complexity without helping the task.
customization: The controller toggles one c-dialog--maximized class and synchronizes aria-pressed.
The original size stays entirely in CSS, so maximizing never stores inline dimensions.
Closing always clears maximized state before the next open.

example.description: Open the dialog, toggle maximize in the header, and restore it before closing.

variants.title: Positioned
variants.summary: The same modal behavior anchored to the top, center, or bottom edge by a trigger option.
variants.useWhen: Use a positioned dialog when its placement should preserve visual context near the region that initiated it.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid edge placement if it makes the dialog resemble a toast or drawer and obscures the blocking nature of the task.
customization: data-dialog-position selects a CSS-only placement; JavaScript does not calculate coordinates.
Logical block margins make top and bottom positions easy to adapt for writing modes.
Keep a viewport gutter at every position and retain the modal backdrop.

example.title: Choose the modal position
example.description: Open the dialog at the top, center, or bottom and verify that each position keeps a safe edge gap.

source.html:
Positioned modal

Context stays nearby

The placement changes without changing focus, dismissal, or accessibility behavior.

variants.title: Non-modal
variants.summary: A floating dialog that leaves the rest of the page interactive and does not render a backdrop.
variants.useWhen: Use a non-modal dialog for a small auxiliary tool that can stay open while the user works elsewhere.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid it for decisions that must be completed before the underlying page can safely continue.
customization: The key behavior difference is dialog.show() instead of dialog.showModal().
Position the surface clearly as an auxiliary window and keep a persistent close control.
Do not apply aria-modal because background content remains available.

example.description: Open the notes window, then interact with the background field while it remains visible.

source.html: Quick notes

variants.title: Animated transitions
variants.summary: Fade-scale, slide-up, and drop-in motion pairs for opening and closing the modal.
variants.useWhen: Use a short transition to preserve spatial context and make a modal entering or leaving the top layer easier to follow.
variants.avoidWhen: Avoid decorative or slow motion that delays a focused task, and never make essential content depend on animation completing.
customization: data-dialog-animation selects fade-scale, slide-up, or drop-in without changing the component markup.
Opening and closing use paired keyframes with the same duration and easing so the motion feels reversible.
prefers-reduced-motion: reduce disables all keyframes and transitions while preserving the open and close behavior.

anatomy.name: Trigger

anatomy.name: Dialog

anatomy.name: Header
anatomy.description: An optional eyebrow and required heading that provide the accessible name.

anatomy.name: Body

anatomy.description: A method=dialog form that closes without custom button handlers.

tokens.description: Text shown on the primary action.

tokens.name: --dialog-gutter
tokens.description: Minimum distance from each viewport edge.

accessibility: The native dialog element supplies modal semantics, focus containment, and Escape dismissal.
aria-labelledby and aria-describedby connect the heading and explanation to the dialog.
Focus returns to the opening control after every close path.
The visible focus ring remains available for keyboard users.
component.responsive: The dialog width is capped on larger screens. Below 32rem, actions stack vertically with the safest action last in visual order and first in DOM order.
limitations: Use only one modal interaction at a time; nested dialogs create confusing focus and dismissal behavior.
The confirmation event reports intent but does not perform application-specific work.
Very old browsers without native dialog support require a polyfill, which is intentionally not included.
